clue.text: I catch and hold ball, though quite out of form

definitions.text: I catch and hold ball, though quite out of form

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it held within, so the ball goes inside the jumbled letters
something out of form has lost its shape, so the letters of I and catch are rearranged

parts.note: a ball is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A fielder admits that, though badly off form, they caught and held the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of form' turns I CATCH into CHATIC, and 'hold' puts O (ball) inside it. The whole clue is also the definition: a player quite out of form is all over the place.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone quite out of form plays in a disordered, haphazard way.

clue.text: O'Casey's whole "Paycock" world was in a state of this frame

definitions.text: O'Casey's whole "Paycock" world was in a state of this
definitions.meaning: in Juno and the Paycock, Captain Boyle says the whole world is in a terrible state of disorder, using Irish slang
the supporting framework of a car

explanation.walkthrough: Captain Boyle's line in Sean O'Casey's play 'Juno and the Paycock' is 'the whole worl's in a terr...ible state o' chassis', his mispronunciation of chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Boyle's word for chaos in O'Casey's play, and the base framework of a motor vehicle.

clue.text: T.T. for Tar Tinter

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, an AB (able seaman)
a tinter colours things, as a stainer does

explanation.surface: Teetotal pledge stated by a man who paints with tar.
explanation.walkthrough: T.T. is teetotal, a person who drinks no alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: T.T. stands for teetotal, describing someone who refuses all alcohol.

clue.text: Wood-obscurers

parts.note: the saying is that you cannot see the wood for these

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says you cannot see the wood for them: the individual plants hide the forest.

clue.text: Bearded island wheat in the Tropics

parts.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples
corn is a word for wheat

explanation.surface: A bearded grain grows on an island in the tropics.
explanation.walkthrough: Capricorn is the goat of the zodiac, hence bearded; 'in the Tropics' points to the Tropic of Capricorn.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac sign is a goat, an animal with a beard, and gives its name to a southern tropic.

clue.text: Old verse tale, like Aesop's, but without point, one windless August

indicators.note: without means lacking, so one letter is dropped from the word for Aesop's stories

parts.note: Aesop's tales are fables
E, east, is a point of the compass
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: windless means with no wind, so the gust is taken out of the month

explanation.surface: A description of an old moral tale that lacks a point and is set in a still summer month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes E from FABLE; 'windless' takes GUST from AUGUST, leaving AU.
explanation.definitionFit: A fabliau is a comic, often bawdy, medieval French tale in verse.

clue.text: Light strike in the picture palace

definitions.meaning: a quick light blow, as with a finger
a picture palace was a cinema, where you see a film

explanation.definitionFit: A quick light flip of the fingers, and slang for a film shown at the cinema.

clue.text: Tapped for a drop of wet perhaps

definitions.text: Tapped for a drop of wet perhaps

parts.words: Tapped for a drop of wet perhaps
parts.note: the glass is tapped to see whether its reading falls, warning of rain

explanation.surface: A barrel tapped for a little drink.
explanation.definitionFit: People tap the weather glass to see if the needle drops, a sign of rain coming.

clue.text: More than one ghost writer

parts.note: the playwright wrote 'Ghosts', so he wrote of more than one ghost

explanation.surface: A celebrity using several hired writers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian playwright wrote the play 'Ghosts'.

clue.text: Reverse James ghost story ?

parts.note: Henry James wrote 'The Turn of the Screw'; to turn a screw the opposite way takes it out

explanation.surface: A request to retell a Henry James ghost tale backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry James's tale is 'The Turn of the Screw'; turning a screw backwards loosens it.

clue.text: Path to which Lover's Lane leads?

definitions.text: Path to which Lover's Lane leads?

parts.words: Path to which Lover's Lane leads?
parts.note: courting couples in a lovers' lane end up walking down the church passage to be married

explanation.surface: A question about where a romantic country lane comes out.
explanation.definitionFit: Courtship leads to a wedding, where the bride walks up the church's central passage.

clue.text: Obviously, not those associated with the raptures of vice

definitions.text: Obviously, not those associated with the raptures of vice

parts.words: Obviously, not those associated with the raptures of vice
parts.note: Swinburne wrote of 'the roses and raptures of vice'; flowers that are prudish would be the opposite of those

explanation.surface: A pointed remark about which pleasures do not go with sin.
explanation.walkthrough: The allusion is Swinburne's line 'the lilies and languors of virtue / the roses and raptures of vice'. Roses that are prim are obviously not those roses.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words, prim roses are prudish flowers, the reverse of Swinburne's roses of vice; whole, they are the pale spring flowers.

clue.text: This comedy can't but be a hit

definitions.text: This comedy can't but be a hit

parts.words: This comedy can't but be a hit
parts.note: a hit is both a success and a blow; knockabout comedy is all blows

explanation.surface: A producer's boast that a new comedy is bound to succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: Knockabout farce is built on blows, named after the clattering stick of the harlequin.

clue.text: One employed to unpick seams?

parts.note: seams sound like needlework, but here they are layers of coal dug out underground

explanation.surface: A job advertisement for a seamstress who takes garments apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A collier works coal seams, taking them apart underground.

clue.text: Al's boy

parts.note: Al Jolson's famous song was addressed to his little boy, using a familiar name for a lad

explanation.walkthrough: Al Jolson's hit song of 1928 was 'Sonny Boy'.
explanation.definitionFit: A familiar way to address a young lad, made famous by Jolson's song title.

clue.text: Shout urgently to someone at the wishing-well, did Goldie ?

definitions.text: Shout urgently to someone at the wishing-well, did Goldie

parts.words: Shout urgently to someone at the wishing-well, did Goldie
parts.note: split up, the word sounds like yelling 'O, wish!' at a well; Goldie, a golden eagle, is gold-coloured

explanation.surface: A scene at a wishing-well where someone named Goldie calls out urgently.
explanation.walkthrough: Goldie was a golden eagle that escaped from London Zoo in 1965 and made the news. The word breaks into YELL, O and WISH.
explanation.definitionFit: A golden bird is close to yellow in colour; the word splits into a shout and a wish.

clue.text: Beat with six no 'balls ?

parts.note: in cricket an over was six balls
a ball thrown rather than bowled is called a no-ball in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: a bowler wins despite an over of illegal deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six deliveries, and a delivery thrown instead of bowled is a no-ball. With 'with' as a link, an over of throws makes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat an opponent is to defeat or topple them.

clue.text: Neither here nor there

parts.note: the idiom means irrelevant, but read literally it means in some other place

explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere that is not here and not there is in another place.

clue.text: Alcoholic goat aggressive 'in the kitchen ?

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic spirit
an aggressive goat butts, so it is a butter

explanation.surface: A drunken, aggressive goat runs riot in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum butter is a sweet spread of butter, sugar and rum, a Cumbrian speciality.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet spread made in the kitchen from butter, sugar and spirit.

clue.text: Tough impot for some luckless lad ?'

parts.note: tough means hard
an impot (imposition) is a school punishment of writing lines

explanation.surface: A schoolboy is given a harsh writing punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: An impot is old British school slang for a punishment of copying out lines. The phrase is also what you say to someone unlucky.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a British exclamation of sympathy for bad luck, said to an unlucky person.

clue.text: Chief executioner dropping a point

indicators.note: dropping means letting go of, so a letter falls out of the executioner's title

parts.note: a headsman beheaded the condemned
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: The chief executioner lets a point slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' takes S (a compass point) out of HEADSMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The leader of a village or tribe is its head figure.

clue.text: Avuncular founder

definitions.meaning: Uncle ... is the elderly storyteller of Joel Chandler Harris's tales
with Romulus, he founded Rome in legend

explanation.definitionFit: Uncle of the Brer Rabbit stories, and the twin who with Romulus was a legendary founder of Rome.

clue.text: Us topsy-turvy' steeplejacks make you' sigh

indicators.note: topsy-turvy means upside down, so in a down clue the word is turned over

parts.note: taken as written
steeplejacks climb a spire

explanation.surface: Watching steeplejacks working upside down makes us gasp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topsy-turvy' turns US into SU; a spire is what steeplejacks climb.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspire is a literary word for to breathe out deeply.

clue.text: Sent on this Valentine is gone to find favour.

indicators.note: a name that is gone has been taken away, so it is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: favour means approval
Val is short for Valentine

explanation.surface: A Valentine card sent in the hope of winning someone's favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is gone' removes VAL (Valentine) from APPROVAL. Goods sent 'on appro' are sent to try before buying.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods sent for trial before purchase are said to be sent on approval, shortened in British usage.

clue.text: So turn up in a cheaper seat we assume

indicators.note: in means the reversed word sits within the seat

parts.note: the pit was the cheaper seating in a theatre

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning a word up reads it from the bottom

explanation.surface: Someone assumes a theatregoer will turn up in a cheap seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' makes SO into OS, and 'in' puts it inside PIT, the cheap seats of an old theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward as a premise, to suppose.

clue.text: Strike, troubles produced by mechanical saws ?

definitions.text: Strike, troubles produced by mechanical saws

parts.words: Strike, troubles produced by mechanical saws
parts.note: a strike at the power station causes loss of electricity; the phrase also reads as cuts made by power saws

explanation.surface: A list of workplace troubles caused by industrial action and machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: Electricity interruptions are blackouts, which strikes cause; read literally they are cuts made with powered saws.

clue.text: Chequered pattern of Welsh nationalism

definitions.meaning: ... Cymru is the Welsh nationalist party

explanation.definitionFit: A tartan cloth, and the Welsh nationalist party Plaid Cymru.

clue.text: Quick, shoot it!

definitions.meaning: a canoeist shoots a fast-flowing stretch of river

explanation.definitionFit: Fast, and a stretch of white water that a boat may shoot.

clue.text: To consume meats I act thus, otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters are arranged differently

explanation.surface: Someone explains how they eat meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges MEATS I ACT. 'thus' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To chew food is the first step in eating it.

clue.text: A little pie, say for the diva ?

indicators.note: say means as it would be spoken, so the word for the pie is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a patty is a small pie

explanation.surface: Someone offers a small pie to a great singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Adelina Patti was a celebrated 19th-century soprano.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelina Patti was a famous opera soprano, a prima donna.

clue.text: Cut to tally

parts.note: scores were kept by cutting marks on a tally stick

explanation.definitionFit: Marks were nicked into a stick to keep count, so a nicked stick records a score.

clue.text: Confirm that the also ran was out of breath

indicators.note: to be out of something is to have none left, so the breathy letter is dropped

parts.note: an also-ran is the horse at the end of the race, an end horse
H is the aspirate, the breathing sound

explanation.surface: Confirming that the losing racehorse was exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was out of' takes H (the breath sound) from END HORSE, the horse at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a statement is to back or approve it.
